# Workspace rules

This repo is one of the git repos in Shawn's Property Analyzer workspace. Local sessions load these rules
from the workspace folder; cloud sessions clone this repo alone, so they are copied in here.

**Paths below are relative to the workspace folder**, which holds every repo side by side. In a
cloud session only this repo is present: `launch-picker/src/report.py` is `src/report.py` when
this repo is launch-picker, and a path into another repo does not exist at all.

## In a cloud session

You have the code, not the data or the machines. Not here: gitignored data (REALIS pulls, the
layout-study database, price-gap pages, brochure PDFs), the Raspberry Pi, deploy credentials,
and Shawn's memory.

- **Never deploy.** Finish on a pushed branch. Say in one line what has to be run on the Mac
  afterwards (a rebuild, `publish.sh`, a deploy) — Shawn pulls and runs it there.
- **Never produce a figure from data that is not in the repo**, and never invent a stand-in for
  it. If the job needs the data, stop and say so.
- **Never edit a generated file to fake a result** — change its generator and say it needs a
  regenerate on the Mac.

## Working in this workspace

### Design and UI work: use impeccable

Three design skills are available and they overlap. Route design work like this:

- **`impeccable` is primary.** All UI/UX review, critique, audit, and improvement work
  goes through it — `critique`, `audit`, `polish`, `bolder`, `layout`, `typeset`,
  `clarify`, `harden`. Both sites here are existing built interfaces, which is what it
  is for.
- **`ui-ux-pro-max` is a lookup only.** Query it for a specific decision that needs
  options — a font pairing, a palette, a chart type. Do not use it to review or
  restructure an existing page; it is a search database, not a reviewer.
- **`frontend-design` is off.** Do not invoke it. It duplicates the other two and adds
  nothing here. (It is an account-synced skill, so it cannot be removed from disk —
  just don't call it.)

Decided by Shawn, 2026-08-19.

### The two UI surfaces are structurally different

- `kya-maps-calculator/index.html` is **hand-authored**, ~15,000 lines, edited in place.
  Serve it with the `kya-calculator` launch config (port 8765) to see changes live.
- `launch-picker/out/report.html` is **generated output** — `launch-picker/src/report.py`
  writes it, with the CSS embedded in the Python. Never edit the HTML; the next run
  overwrites it. Design changes go in `report.py`, then regenerate.
- `kya-maps-calculator/launch/index.html` is **that same generated file**, copied in by
  `launch-picker/publish.sh` and framed by the calculator's **Launch Day Strategy** tab.
  It is committed here so the advisory site deploys on its own, but it is NOT authored
  here: edit `report.py` and re-publish. The tab loads it with `?embed=1`, which drops the
  report's own brand bar so the page carries one identity bar (`html.embed` in report.py).
  `launch/meta.json` beside it carries the build date the tab prints as its "as at" stamp.

  One command keeps both sites in step:

  ```bash
  cd launch-picker && ./publish.sh
  ```

Product context for the calculator is in `kya-maps-calculator/PRODUCT.md`. There is no
`DESIGN.md` yet for either site.

### COMPULSORY: the stack category table, after every site plan, before any figures

**Shawn, 2026-09-05: *"I want you to make sure IT IS COMPULSORY for all agents to give it to me
after EVERY site plan, BEFORE gathering the data and tabulating the figures."***

This applies to every agent and every project in the facing / stack study
(`launch-picker/stack-study`). It is a GATE, not a courtesy:

1. Read the site plan and measure the geometry off OSM.
2. **STOP. Put the view table to Shawn and wait for his audit.**
3. Only after he has ruled: build the facings file, run `assign_types.py`, `premium.py`,
   `cutoff.py`, `certainty.py`, `stack_embed.py`.

Running the numbers first and showing him the categories afterwards is the failure this rule
exists to stop — by then the figures are already anchored on categories he has not checked.

#### THE SHAPE OF THE TABLE — ONE ROW PER VIEW, STACKS COMBINED

**Shawn, 2026-09-06, and this SUPERSEDES the one-row-per-stack instruction of 2026-09-01 and
2026-09-05: *"I want you to ALWAYS make sure you have an inward facing view. And i want you to
combine the stacks together so its easy to read. Basically only few rows are required, with
combining of stacks into one view. so only 4 rows or so is required."***

| view (the category, as it displays on the page) | stacks | what is in the sightline | break |
|---|---|---|---|

* **ONE ROW PER VIEW, not per stack.** Four to six rows for a whole project. Every stack that
  lands in the same cell goes on one line as a stack list.
* **THERE MUST ALWAYS BE AN INWARD FACING VIEW.** Every project has one and it is the baseline
  every other figure is measured against. If the read produces no inward row, the read is wrong —
  go back and find it before showing him anything.
* the category in **both forms** — the key (`road|open-low-rise`) and the name as it DISPLAYS on
  the stack analysis page ("Road + unblocked view (landed facing)").
* the **height break** — the floor at which the view changes, and what causes it. Say **which
  storey counts are MEASURED and which are ESTIMATED**; an estimated height is an estimated break
  and that is what he is auditing.

The point of the earlier one-row-per-stack rule still stands and is met by this shape: he is
auditing WHICH CELL each stack lands in, and a stack list per cell shows that just as exactly
while fitting on one screen. Distances and storey counts are the EVIDENCE for the category — they
go in the sightline column or the facings file's `beyond` field, never in place of the category.

See `launch-picker/stack-study/README.md` and the `show-the-category-not-the-sightline` memory.

### COMPULSORY: the layout method, before any development's layout figures

**Shawn, 2026-09-18: *"i need you to remember all these rules that i'm giving you because you need
to replace this order of analysis for ALL development across singapore. make sure the consistency
of measurement is recorded so every agent that does it knows how it is done."***

**`layout-study/docs/METHOD.md` is the procedure.** Read it before measuring what any development
pays for a floor-plan feature. It is not a Treasure at Tampines write-up — it is what every agent
does at every development, in order, with the same constants. `layout-study/TAKEOVER.md` is the
state of the work; METHOD.md is how the work is done.

#### SCOPE — two hard exclusions, both of which he has had to repeat

* **NO 1-BEDROOM. EVERY CLASS STARTS AT 2BR.** Shawn, 2026-09-19: *"i mentioned before, DO NOT
  TOUCH 1BEDROOM, start from 2BR. did you not remember this."* No 1BR, no 1BR+Study — not in the
  size screen, not in a plan read, not in a figure, and 1BR → 2BR is not a crossing worth
  measuring.
* **NO CCR.** *"DON'T TOUCH CCR ... CCR has traditionally been built larger than usual."* Its area
  steps are not the same product step, and the study never adjusts for area. **The region split is
  OCR + RCR.**

#### THE RULE HE HAS GIVEN MOST OFTEN — and he has had to repeat it

> ## NEVER ADJUST FOR AREA.  ALWAYS ADJUST FOR FLOOR AND FACING.

**Shawn, 2026-09-19: *"Because i have said this multiple times on the 'dont adjust for area' and
'always adjust for floor and facing'."*** One rule, two halves.

* **NEVER FOR AREA.** *"a bathroom addition is indeed a bathroom addition, dont adjust anything for
  it. unless the layout differs signficantly."* A feature pair's figure is the **RAW DIFFERENCE**.
  A bathroom arriving with 32 sqft is worth $175,000 (Stirling) and one arriving with 118 sqft is
  worth $250,000 (JadeScape) — that gap is a fact, not an error. "Differs significantly" is already
  tested by the 60% share gate and the circulation guard; fail either and the pair LEAVES the study
  rather than being adjusted.
* **ALWAYS FOR FLOOR AND FACING**, from the **stack facing study** — *"take reference from
  https://kya-launch-picker-offline.pages.dev/ stack facing study that was done to adjust for it."*
  Facing from `launch-picker/stack-study/results/<dev>.json` (band `all`, market **direct** only),
  floor from `layout-study/out/normalisation.json`. Both measured elsewhere on other pairs, never
  fitted to the pairs being measured — that distinction is what withdrew the $27,710.
* **The facing study's unit is `facingType`, so ours is too.** Matching the exact track on
  `facingType` is right. Do not tighten it to the named view or the side: that invents a
  distinction the facing study cannot price. The answer to a coarse cell is a finer FACING study.

The five rulings it enforces, in the order Shawn gave them:

1. **Match, never model — but adjust, and test the adjustment.** TRACK A is the exact match: same
   floor, same facing, ≤183 days, **RESALE ONLY**, raw difference. TRACK B adjusts floor and
   facing with figures **measured elsewhere on other pairs**, and the two are reported side by
   side, never blended. `ADJUSTED_ONLY` uses only the pairs the exact rule discards, so comparing
   them is a real test — it must land within 10%. **A facing premium applies only to the bedroom
   classes it was measured on.** Fitting a residual to the pairs being measured is still banned;
   that is what produced the withdrawn $27,710.
   **Dual key is out of the study entirely** — a different product with a rental-yield term.
2. **A feature is a SIZE, not a tick-box.** ≥80% of the area step must be the added rooms,
   measured off the plans.
3. **The plan beats the developer's label.** Record the conflict when they disagree.
4. **Quote QUANTUM**, not percent, not psf.
5. **NO AREA-ONLY FIGURES, ANYWHERE.** Same feature package on both sides is a price for a square
   foot — dropped from the library outright, never shown.
6. **THE PRODUCT CLASS IS THE UNIT** — `(bedrooms, bathrooms, WC, study)` as the PLAN DRAWS
   it, never the developer's tier name (amended 2026-09-18: Parc Esta prints none). Bedroom
   crossings carry **no sizes**: "3BR2B+WC → 4BR2B", never "1087 → 1238". A size is a fact about one development; a class is a fact about
   the market, and only the class aggregates.

Every constant (tolerances, windows, the 0.80 gate, minimum pair counts, the clustered bootstrap)
is in one table in METHOD.md so no agent re-invents one. **A deviation is recorded in
`data/annotations/<project>.json` under `method_deviations`, with the reason — an unrecorded
deviation makes the figure unusable.**

### Cloud sessions get a copy of these rules

A Claude cloud session clones one GitHub repo and never sees this folder or the memory, so each
repo carries `WORKSPACE-RULES.md` — this file plus `STANDING-RULES.md` — imported by its own
`CLAUDE.md`. **After editing this file or `STANDING-RULES.md`, run `./sync-cloud-rules.sh` and
commit + push the repos it changed.**

## Standing rules — from Shawn's corrections

These live in the local memory, which cloud sessions never see. Each one came from Shawn
correcting an agent; breaking one repeats a mistake he has already paid for.

### Who you are working for

Shawn is a Singapore property agent (KYA Real Estate, PropNex). Everything here answers a
client's question with **measured evidence instead of an opinion**: is this development worth
buying, which stack, which floor, which facing, what will it be worth on exit. He reads the
transactions himself and will ask why a number is what it is.

He is not a software engineer and does not want to be addressed as one. Give him the answer, the
recommendation, and the reason — in that order, in as few words as possible.

### How to report

- **Report the answer, not the working.** Lead with the conclusion; distributions are proof.
- **Every analysis ends in a recommendation** ("go for stack N", "safe either way").
- **No internal acronyms or code names** in anything he reads. Name what the thing does.
- **Never say "executive"** — in Singapore property it means an executive condominium (EC).
- **Say the direction, not just the percentage** — who pays more. Inside 1%, "no difference".
- **Quote quantum ($)** beside any percentage, and a number where a number will do — no ranges.
- **Always split by bedroom** — 2BR / 3BR / 4BR+ on every table from the start.

### How to do the work

- **Never compare a dual key unless the unit valued is one.** Dual key against dual key only,
  everything else against everything else, in every comparable set. Which sizes are dual key:
  `kya-maps-calculator/layout-gap/dualkey.json` (RealSmart unit mix); a size that only *may* be dual
  key stays out too.
- **Matched pairs, never averages.** A premium comes from matched transaction pairs, never from
  differencing two band medians.
- **Never infer observed data.** Read every case against its source — a site plan, floor plan or
  caveat decides, not the pattern you expect.
- **Never exclude projects.** Every development must stay findable; never filter one out of a
  roster because its data is thin.
- **Never retract published work.** If a figure on a client page looks thin, measure the
  thinness and tell him. Deciding what a client sees is his call.
- **Remove means remove.** Remove exactly what he named and leave the slot empty — never let a
  selection rule pull in a replacement. If the target could be read two ways, ask.
- **Ask before spending.** Any run that costs money (model calls, paid APIs) needs his yes, and
  "ok run" authorises that one run only.
- **Ignore Lentor Gardens and Dunearn House** — no launch-report work, tests or mentions.

### Client pages

- **As little text as possible.** The standing view carries figures and labels; a sentence moves
  one tap behind the explain mark rather than being deleted.
- **Refine, never redesign.** The navy-and-gold identity stays; fixes happen inside it.
- **Read on a 1024pt iPad.** Nothing short may wrap.
- **The sites are deliberately offline-safe.** Never add a CDN or third-party fetch.
- **One template, every launch.** A launch-report change is made once in `report.py` and shows on
  every launch; never a project-specific branch for a display feature.
